cards.text: Isaiah the prophet (Isaiah 1:1) just finished a burden against the Philistines. Now here comes the next one: the burden against Moab, the nation that came from Lot's son Moab (Genesis 19:37). It opens with two Moab towns, Ar and Kir, and the news moves FAST. Faster than a group chat, friend.

cards.question: Ar in Moab is ruined, and Kir in Moab is devastated. Each one is destroyed in a ___.

cards.text: Now the grief spreads from town to town. "Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places."

cards.question: Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba, and every head is shaved. What happens to every beard in Moab?

cards.text: Every beard, cut off. I'd hold my mustache a little closer right now, friend, but my mustache IS my hands.

cards.question: Moab wears sackcloth in the streets, and Heshbon and Elealeh cry out so loud they're heard as far as Jahaz. Through all this, Moab's soldiers stay calm and steady.
This is a burden against Moab. But as the speaker looks at Moab's ruin, what does the speaker's heart do?

cards.text: A heart crying out over Moab. You expected a victory party, and you got THAT. Meanwhile her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, weeping up the slope of Luhith on the road to Horonaim.

cards.question: As Moab's people flee, the waters of Nimrim are dried up.
Around Nimrim the grass is withered and the greenery is gone. What do Moab's people carry over the Brook of the Willows?

cards.text: Their outcry echoes to the border of Moab, all the way to Eglaim and Beer-elim. When a whole nation cries, the neighbors hear it.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood. Then the message says, "I will bring more upon Dimon" and friend, it's not done yet.

cards.question: More is coming upon Dimon. What will come upon the fugitives of Moab and the remnant of the land?

cards.text: Then comes a command: "Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land" all the way from Sela in the desert.

cards.question: The tribute lambs are sent from Sela in the desert. Where are they sent to?

cards.text: The daughters of Moab are at the fords of the Arnon, like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest. I know that feeling, friend. My nest was a cookie counter, and I landed in a junk drawer.

cards.question: The daughters of Moab stand at the fords of the Arnon and plead. What do they ask for?
The prophecy looks ahead to when the oppressor has gone and destruction has ceased. Where will a throne be established in loving devotion?
A judge will sit on that throne in faithfulness, seeking ___ and hastening righteousness.

cards.text: Then the tone shifts again. "We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance."

cards.question: Moab is full of pride and conceit. But the prophecy says his boasting is ___.

cards.text: Empty boasting. The dead batteries I shared that drawer with swore EVERY day they still had a little charge left. Friend, they did NOT.

cards.question: Moab moans for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, and the fields of Heshbon and the grapevines of Sibmah have withered.

cards.text: Those vines of Sibmah had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Then the rulers of the nations trampled the choicest ones.

cards.question: The harvest is ruined and the best vines are trampled. How does the speaker respond to the vines of Sibmah?

cards.text: Joy is gone from the orchard, and no one sings or tramples the grapes anymore. Then the message says, "I have put an end to the cheering."

cards.question: After all this, the speaker's heart still laments for Moab like a harp.

cards.text: Moab heads up to the high place, wears himself out, and goes into his sanctuary to pray.

cards.question: Moab wears himself out and prays in his sanctuary. What will it do for him?

answers.text: It will do him no good
It will turn the destroyer back
It will bring back the harvest

cards.text: This is the message the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab. And now the LORD adds a timeline.

cards.question: The LORD says Moab's splendor will become an object of contempt in ___ years.

cards.text: Three years, "as a hired worker counts the years" and friend, NOBODY counts time closer than somebody on the clock at 4:59.

cards.question: When those three years are done, the people left in Moab will be many and strong.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Isaiah the prophet...', 'Now here comes the next one...', 'It opens with two Moab towns...', and 'Faster than a group chat, friend.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: 'the news moves FAST. Faster than a group chat' tells the baker the destruction is quick. That rules out 'month' and 'year' on card 2, so only 'night' is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The group chat joke compares news spreading fast to towns being destroyed in a night. These are different actions. The verse is about how quickly the towns fall, not how quickly word travels.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'just finished a burden against the Philistines' is a Bible fact with no reference (Isaiah 14:28-32). Also, 'Isaiah the prophet (Isaiah 1:1)' cites a verse that never calls Isaiah a prophet. Isaiah 37:2 does.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This card only repeats card 4's answer ('Every beard, cut off') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'When a whole nation cries, the neighbors hear it' adds a fact. Isaiah 15:8 says the outcry echoes to the border of Moab and reaches Eglaim and Beer-elim. It never says anyone beyond Moab hears it.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The card quotes an 'I' line ('I will bring more upon Dimon') but only says 'the message says', so the speaker is never named. Isaiah 16:13 identifies this as the message the LORD spoke.

rule.text: Who's speaking. When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: This card only repeats card 8's answer ('Empty boasting') and adds the batteries joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The true statement includes the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, which come from Isaiah 16:7. The card cites only Isaiah 16:8. It should cite Isaiah 16:7-8.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: 'Moab moans for the raisin cakes' turns a command into a report. Isaiah 16:7 is a command: 'Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.' The text never says Moab moans.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card quotes an 'I' line ('I have put an end to the cheering') but only says 'the message says', so the speaker is never named. Isaiah 16:13 identifies this as the message the LORD spoke.

rule.text: Who's speaking. When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: 'And now the LORD adds a timeline' tells Isaiah 16:14 ('And now the LORD says, "In three years...'), but the card cites only Isaiah 16:13. It should cite Isaiah 16:13-14.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
